samples.summary: buildRects' start default flipped from 'backward' to 'forward' for every affinity-less range — this silently changes rendering (and hit-testing) for four out-of-diff consumers of computeSelectionRects that never carry an affinity
samples.evidence: Before this change, the non-cell branch of buildRects resolved BOTH endpoints through findPageForPosition with its 'backward' default (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:385). The diff introduces `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'`, so any range built without endpoint affinity now resolves its start one visual line later at a wrap boundary. Callers that build such ranges and were not touched or considered: comment-marker rects, whose output also backs click hit-testing via commentMarkerRects/getCommentMarkerAt — packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1659-1668; search-match highlights — editor.ts:1638-1651 and the active-match scroll math at editor.ts:3129-3138 (rects[0].y drives container.scrollTop); spell-error underlines + their hit-test cache — editor.ts:1676-1689; peer selections published by a mixed-version/older peer (no lineAffinity on the wire) — editor.ts:1620-1626; and slides text boxes — packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:560. A comment marker or spell error whose start offset sits exactly on a wrap boundary now paints and hit-tests on the next visual line.

samples.summary: Cursor now has two disagreeing affinity sources: `cursor.position.lineAffinity` (new) and `cursor.lineAffinity` (existing). Existing `moveTo(pos)` call sites that omit the second argument leave them contradictory
samples.evidence: Cursor.moveTo assigns `this.position = pos` verbatim and `this.lineAffinity = affinity` (default 'backward') — packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:28-32. The diff makes positions carry their own affinity, so any pre-existing site that passes an affinity-carrying position WITHOUT the second argument desyncs the two: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2789 `this.cursor.moveTo(collapsePos)` (collapsePos is a selection endpoint that now carries the click's 'forward'), text-editor.ts:1544 `this.cursor.moveTo(pos)` (pos is the new affinity-carrying mousedown position), text-editor.ts:2751, and packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3469 `cursor.moveTo(opts.position)`. The caret is then painted from cursor.lineAffinity ('backward', cursor.ts:47-49) while the very next shift+Arrow/shift+click builds its anchor from cursor.position (text-editor.ts:2774, 1620, 1572) and paints the highlight from the stale 'forward' — caret and highlight land on different visual lines.

samples.summary: Peer caret rendering still hardcodes 'backward' while peer selection highlights now honour the published lineAffinity, so a peer's caret and their highlight disagree at a wrap boundary
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1561-1568 calls resolvePositionPixel(peer.position, 'backward', ...) unconditionally, ignoring `peer.position.lineAffinity` that the store now publishes (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:3004 -> packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:226). The same PR routes the peer's selection endpoints through computeSelectionRects, which now honours affinity (editor.ts:1620). The new type comment at packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:24-26 acknowledges this, and docs/tasks/active/20260822-pr-batch-925-931-todo.md:103 lists it as a known gap — but the consumer is left inconsistent.

samples.summary: Doc comment now states the opposite of the new model contract
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/find-position-at-pixel.ts:10-13 reads: "`DocPosition` from `model/types.ts` only carries `{ blockId, offset }`; affinity is a hit-test-derived field ... so it lives on the result type rather than on the model type." The diff adds `lineAffinity?: 'forward' | 'backward'` to DocPosition (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts), so this rationale for PixelPosition existing separately is now false and misleading to the next reader.

samples.summary: The public onCursorMove callback type still declares endpoints as `{ blockId; offset }`, so the frontend subscriber is typed without the field the runtime now carries
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:128 (and the internal CursorMoveCallback alias at editor.ts:1179) type the emitted position and selection endpoints as `{ blockId: string; offset: number }`. At runtime fireCursorMoveCallbacks passes `cursor.position` and `selection.range.anchor/focus` (editor.ts:2069, 1160), which now carry lineAffinity, and the frontend forwards them straight into the widened `updateCursorPos` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:399/407 -> yorkie-doc-store.ts:2972). The affinity survives only by structural accident; the declared contract says it is not there, and packages/frontend has no `tsc` lane to flag a consumer that relies on the declared shape.

samples.summary: Peer-presence dedupe key ignores the newly published lineAffinity
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:283 builds `posKey = `${blockId}:${offset}``. A peer whose caret changes only its affinity (same block/offset, different visual line) now publishes a changed presence that this key treats as unchanged, so the label/refresh path is skipped.

finding.evidence: Before this change, the non-cell branch of buildRects resolved BOTH endpoints through findPageForPosition with its 'backward' default (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:385). The diff introduces `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'`, so any range built without endpoint affinity now resolves its start one visual line later at a wrap boundary. Callers that build such ranges and were not touched or considered: comment-marker rects, whose output also backs click hit-testing via commentMarkerRects/getCommentMarkerAt — packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1659-1668; search-match highlights — editor.ts:1638-1651 and the active-match scroll math at editor.ts:3129-3138 (rects[0].y drives container.scrollTop); spell-error underlines + their hit-test cache — editor.ts:1676-1689; peer selections published by a mixed-version/older peer (no lineAffinity on the wire) — editor.ts:1620-1626; and slides text boxes — packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:560. verdict.reason: The default flip at selection.ts:260 is real, but the claimed blast radius is not. A backward-affinity start on a wrap boundary resolved to the END of the previous line, so the multi-line branch (selection.ts:503-534) emitted a ZERO-WIDTH first rect there and still emitted the full next-line rect — the repo's own test asserts exactly this ("a zero-width tail on line 0 plus all of line 1", selection-line-affinity.test.ts:104-115). Therefore every listed consumer sees identical visible geometry: painting is fillRect(x,y,width,h)/squigglePoints(x,width,...) (doc-canvas.ts:405-447), so a zero-width rect drew nothing; comment hit-testing uses strict `x < r.x + r.width` (comment-markers.ts:39-45), so a zero-width rect was never hittable, leaving getCommentMarkerAt (editor.ts:3261-3263) unchanged; spell hit-testing does not use the rects at all — getSpellErrorAt goes through paginatedPixelToPosition/spellSession.errorAt (editor.ts:3174-3180) and getSpellErrorRects (editor.ts:3160) has no consumer anywhere. The only genuine delta is rects[0].y in the active-match scroll math (editor.ts:3136-3148), which now scrolls to the visual line the match text actually occupies — a one-line cosmetic shift, not a broken caller, and explicitly reasoned about in the task doc (20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:18-26). No bypassed guard, no broken contract, no violated invariant under this lens's rubric.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: Cursor.moveTo (cursor.ts:28-32) copies the position verbatim but sets this.lineAffinity from the parameter (default 'backward'), and caret painting reads only cursor.lineAffinity (cursor.ts:47-49 via resolvePositionPixel, peer-cursor.ts:97-104). Meanwhile DocPosition now carries lineAffinity (model/types.ts:200-214) and selection painting honors it (selection.ts:260-261), with normalizeRange returning endpoints as stored (selection.ts:166-180). Concrete desync sites exist: handleMouseDown builds an affinity-carrying pos (text-editor.ts:1521-1525) and calls moveTo(pos) with no affinity at text-editor.ts:1544; the collapse path calls moveTo(collapsePos) at text-editor.ts:2789 where collapsePos can carry 'forward'; also text-editor.ts:2751. The stale affinity is then read back as a selection endpoint via pos = this.cursor.position (text-editor.ts:2455) at text-editor.ts:2774/1620/1572, so the next shift+Arrow/shift+click paints the highlight endpoint from an affinity that contradicts the painted caret. No guard normalizes affinity off cursor.position. Only the editor.ts:3469 site is spurious (opts.position is typed {blockId, offset} at editor.ts:3461), which does not undermine the finding. In-lane for blast-radius (changed contract, unupdated callers) and reachable, so major/blocking.

finding.summary: Resolved caret `lineAffinity` is dropped by the only production consumer: `restoreLocalCursor` rebuilds the position without the field and calls `cursor.moveTo(pos)` with no affinity argument

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present. `restoreLocalCursor` at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3592-3611 explicitly threads the resolved affinity through: it spreads `lineAffinity` onto the position object (line 3603-3605) AND passes `cursorPos.lineAffinity` as `moveTo`'s second argument (line 3607), with a comment stating exactly why ("dropping it here would undo the anchor round-trip and re-collapse the caret onto the previous visual line at a wrap boundary"). `Cursor.moveTo` (packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:28-31) assigns that argument to `this.lineAffinity`, so the affinity resolved by `resolveAnchoredLocalCursor()` and consumed at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:368-371 survives, and cannot disagree with the affinity broadcast by `publishResolvedLocalCursor` at docs-view.tsx:375. The finding's quoted snippet (`cursor.moveTo({ blockId, offset: Math.min(...) })` with no affinity) does not exist at that location. The only remaining case is `cursorPos.lineAffinity === undefined`, where moveTo applies its documented 'backward' default — and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:972 likewise omits the key when absent, so presence and local render stay consistent. The proposed fix ("pass cursorPos.lineAffinity through to moveTo") is already implemented.

finding.summary: Undo/redo selection restore strips endpoint `lineAffinity`, which the new start-defaults-to-'forward' rule turns from harmless into a rendering change
finding.evidence: `restoreSelectionFromPresence`'s local `clampPos` returns `{ blockId, offset }` only (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1974-1978), discarding the `lineAffinity` that `getPresenceSelection()` now returns on each endpoint (published by yorkie-doc-store.ts:3005 via `anchorDocRange`/`clampPosToModel`, and typed in packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:33-34). Previously dropping it was inert because every consumer defaulted to `'backward'`; this PR's documented default (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:200-206, implemented at packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260) makes an affinity-less START read `'forward'`. So an undo-restored selection whose start was recorded with an explicit `'backward'` affinity at a wrap boundary now paints beginning on the following visual line instead of where the user selected. Fix on `clampPos`: spread the endpoint's `lineAffinity` through.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the tree. `clampPos` in `restoreSelectionFromPresence` returns only `{ blockId, offset }` (editor.ts:1974-1978) and is applied to both endpoints (editor.ts:1989-1990) before `selection.setRange` (editor.ts:1995) on the undo (editor.ts:2022) and redo (editor.ts:2048) paths. The presence selection it reads genuinely carries `lineAffinity`: it is typed on `activeSelection.anchor/focus` (frontend/src/types/users.ts:29-34), preserved by `clampPosToModel` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:972) and published by `updateCursorPos` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2991-3006), which `setCursorForHistory` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2878-2884) flushes with the live `selection.range` (editor.ts:1953) so Yorkie records it as the undo reverse; `getPresenceSelection()` returns that shape (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2937-2952). Endpoints do receive explicit affinity in normal interaction (text-editor.ts:1521-1526, 1773-1778, 1795-1799) and `Selection` keeps them verbatim (selection.ts:685-692, 703-711). Because the start now defaults to 'forward' when affinity is absent (selection.ts:260, contract documented at model/types.ts:200-213), a restored start that was recorded 'backward' at a wrap boundary paints on the following visual line. No guard elsewhere re-attaches affinity after the restore, and the change's own plan says undo/redo restore should keep it (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:49-52). This is a consumer of the changed default left un-updated — squarely in the blast-radius lane.
